newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - Russia restates EU membership ambitions.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Russia restates EU membership ambitions.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, just two days after the European Union opened the historic process of taking in states from behind the former Iron Curtain, said on Friday Russia too was set on joining.

"In the near future, I think that Russia should be in the EU with all the implications and consequences, not all of which will be easy for us," Chernomyrdin told a news conference according to the official English translation.
Russian speakers at the press conference said Chernomyrdin made no reference to a time element, and the Russian Mission to the EU was unable to resolve the discrepancy.
Chernomyrdin, speaking after meeting European Commission President Jacques Santer, was restating ambitions already voiced by President Boris Yeltsin.
He said Russia's dealings with the EU had one goal, "to become equal partners in this continent."

"Yes indeed...I think that our work here, our entire scope of work, all issues and problems that we are discussing, are directed to one objective, that at a certain point Russia will become a member of the EU," he said.

This week the Commission recommended to EU governments that the Union open membership talks with five out of 10 eastern European applicants -- Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia and Estonia.

But it said that five other countries, including two former members of the Soviet Union -- Latvia and Lithuania -- along with Bulgaria, Romania and Slovakia were far from prepared to open entry talks.

Russia has not formally applied for EU membership, and the Commission avoided broaching the prospect in its giant policy blueprint, Agenda 2000, published on Wednesday to propel the bloc into the next century.

Russia virulently opposed the separate expansion plans of the NATO military alliance, which at a historic summit on July 8 agreed to invite three of its former Warsaw Pact allies -- Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to entry talks.
Santer did not directly address Russia's EU membership ambitions during the press conference.

But, in reply to a question about whether Russia was deemed to have achieved a market economy -- one of the main conditions for joining the EU -- he said he had "every confidence that the reforms already started by the Russian authorities will bear fruit."
He said Russia's economic progress would be improved further by its planned accession to the World Trade Organisation.
Privately Commission officials cast doubt after the statement on the capability of the European bloc to absorb its giant eastern neighbour, which stretches right across Asia.
"The question is -- who will be joining whom?" said one.
Chernomyrdin said that membership took precedence over any ambitions to seek compensation from the wealthy western bloc for a future EU enlargement to some of Moscow's main trading parters.
"Compensation is not a top priority for us," he said.

EU states, which will discuss the Commission's recommended invitation list for the first time in Brussels on Tuesday at a meeting of EU foreign ministers, will have final say over the extent of the EU's first eastern enlargement.
